topics.topic: Complete typed field declarations and optionality for every State 1 model
questions: Replace the deferral with declarations of every field of each State 1 model and its type in this state.
Replace the deferral of model field names, types, and formal optionality with complete typed field declarations for every model fact in this state.
Replace the deferral of model field names and types with declarations of every field and its type for each model specified in State 1.

quotes: Field names, types, formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0, "Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).

SPEC_STANDARD §5's rule that every field is declared with its type is a rule of the specification's `models` section, and that section is State 6's output (`skills/spec-authoring/AUTHORING_SEQUENCE.md`): State 6 writes each model here with every fact as a typed field, and declares there what this state decides — its identity and its kind (§5, §15.1.1).
judgement.why: Complete field names, types and formal optionality are expressly assigned to State 6, so §5 governs that later models output rather than this State 1 domain-fact inventory.

topics.topic: Authority responsible for creating imported Room records and writing their copied names
questions: Who creates an imported Room record, and who counts as the writer of its copied name: the legacy writer, the owner who checks and confirms the import, or the migration closure, given that R0-96 says the import writes no name of its own?
Who creates or writes a Room record brought in by the migration import: the import/migration closure, the owner who confirms the import, or one of the two writers named here?

judgement.why: P2 already judged the same question on the same import, Room and copied-name passages, which have not changed.

precedent.topic: Creator and name-writer provenance for Rooms stored by import
quotes: | import projects with their identity | owner, confirming, from the VPS instance: the projects the owner picks (R0-79), each with a new display name and alias when the owner gives them (R0-85) | those projects under the identities they carry, with their customers, objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact (R0-34, R0-44, R0-50); a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`, the old value moving to its tax id when it is one, and its projects are linked to that Customer (R0-80) | any conflict with an id production holds refuses the whole import, nothing applied, and the owner may retry after correcting it; after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused (R0-79) |

Facts: `room_id`, minted by Registry or kept by the import; its name, as its
writer wrote it (R0-68); its project; written once: the instant it was added
and the request id of its create, as the caller gave it (R0-36; owner,
2026-10-31, State 2 A01), absent for a room the import brought in.

The import then copies names the
owner has already checked; it writes no name of its own and refuses none.
precedent.why: The owner-confirmed import is the product action that creates the production Rooms while retaining their identities, and it copies each source-written name without becoming that name's writer.

topics.topic: Required added instant and request ID semantics for imported Rooms
questions: What value does an imported Room carry as its required added instant: the legacy creation instant, the instant of successful import, or no instant?
For an imported Room, is only the create request id absent, or are both the added instant and the request id absent; if the instant exists, is it copied from the source or minted at import?

quotes:
A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: a
  project's created, last-changed and archived instants, a room's added
  instant, a pointer's published and superseded instants. Its revision starts
  at 1, the v1 Registry having none (R0-35). A Customer the import makes is
  created at the import's instant with revision 1.

Facts: `room_id`, minted by Registry or kept by the import; its name, as its
writer wrote it (R0-68); its project; written once: the instant it was added
and the request id of its create, as the caller gave it (R0-36; owner,
2026-10-31, State 2 A01), absent for a room the import brought in.
judgement.why: An imported Room keeps the source's added instant, while the create request id is absent.

topics.topic: Authoritative source for AccessRequest after Kernel initiates its creation or replacement
questions: Is Kernel's call merely the event that creates or replaces an AccessRequest, while Registry's embedded AgentSession value is authoritative thereafter, or must Kernel remain the authoritative source when the request is read?

quotes:
An agent session's ask, in free text, for a further project (R0-47). The owner
sees it in the owner interface and answers it from the catalogue; either
answer clears it (R0-64). A session holds at most one; a newer one replaces it
(R0-46). Registry keeps no reason for a decline and no history of requests
(R0-64).
Embedded in the AgentSession record while pending.
judgement.why: Kernel's call originates the value, but Registry persists the pending value inside AgentSession and supplies it to the owner interface thereafter.

topics.topic: Authority for minting project_id in test instances and whether callers may supply it
questions: Who mints `project_id` when a Project is created in a test instance, and is a caller ever allowed to supply it there?

quotes:
A caller may give the `project_id` when creating a project. A repeated create
with that id and equal content returns the existing project; with different
content it is refused, and nothing changes. Without an id the server still
mints one. One physical object can therefore carry one id across instances
(R0-05). V1-5 ("MUST NOT reuse caller-supplied identifiers") is replaced.

Narrowed by R0-34 (an id crosses into production only by an explicit import),
R0-36 (a create without an id is replay-safe too) and R0-44 (in production
Registry mints every id on create; a caller-supplied id enters only by import).
judgement.why: Outside production, a caller may supply project_id, while the test Registry mints one when the caller omits it; R0-44 restricts caller-supplied identities only in production.

precedent.topic: Whether AccessRequest creation time is part of value identity
quotes:
Facts: the text, as the agent wrote it (R0-68: a value that names a person is
not refused); written once: the instant it was made.

Substitution: a request is reached only through its session, and a session's
pending request is whichever was made last; a new request with the same text
replaces the pending one like any other and nothing distinguishes the two. Continuity: none — it is replaced whole or cleared,
never corrected, and leaves no trace of its own (R0-64).
precedent.why: Both passages appear unchanged in the closed and reopened State 1 texts, and the intervening change did not touch AccessRequest or make its value-identity treatment newly consequential.

topics.topic: Whether ArtifactPointer stores an immutable owner service or derives it from mutable type vocabulary
questions: Does each ArtifactPointer carry an immutable owner-service fact fixed at publication/import, or does it carry only its type and derive the owner service from a vocabulary that may later remove or change that type?

quotes:
Every pointer — published, superseded, withdrawn, of removed types too —
each with every fact M05 holds but its request id (Conventions): id,
project, type, version, status, owner service, `uri`, `payload_ref`, digest, publisher and published instant, the
superseded instant, the withdrawing principal and withdrawn instant; by type,
then version highest first, then pointer id.

A type never changes its owner service; a move is a removal and a new type.
   A removed type's name is never declared again, so its history never
   continues.
judgement.why: State 5 lists owner service as a stored pointer fact even for removed types, while State 2 makes the type-to-owner association immutable and forbids reusing a removed type name.

topics.topic: Whether Room needs merge and split lifecycle status, replacement references, and filtering
questions: Does Room permanently have no status and no merge/split lifecycle, or must it have a final merged/superseded status, a replacement-room reference, and current-room filtering?

quotes:
None: created, never changed, never removed (R0-10). It goes with the
project's anonymisation or deletion (R0-62).

Merging and splitting rooms (owner, 2026-10-31): a real planner scenario
  that R0-10 does not allow — a room is never renamed or removed. Until a
  consumer needs it, the planner merges by adding a new room and moving its own
  documents; the old rooms and every reference to them stay. When the planner
  needs it, the candidate is a room status after M05's pattern — `merged` (or
  superseded) with a reference to the room that replaces it, lists showing
  current rooms — as a new decision on R0-10. Does not block State 2.
judgement.why: The current design gives Room no merge or split lifecycle: a planner adds a new Room and all old Rooms remain, while any supersession status would require a future State 0 decision.
